bib.title: Retrieval-augmented reasoning with lean language models

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning with Lean Language Models", Chan, Nanni, Lazauskas, Wood, Yong, Tarassenko, Girolami, Geddes, Duncan (Alan Turing Institute et al.). arXiv:2508.11386v1, technical report (preprint), 2025-08-15. Code: github.com/alan-turing-institute/t0-1.

COVERAGE: Extraction was clean text. All 100,437 chars were extracted. I read body, discussion, conclusion, and the appendix start (A.1-A.3) and tail (A.5, A.6.1). I skimmed references only for origins. I did not read the middle and end of the appendix: A.4 (synthetic-query prompt), A.6.2-A.6.4 (more evaluation prompts). These are prompt templates. Fig. 2 and Fig. 5 values are plotted only, and no numbers are in the text for them.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. A 32B model fine-tuned on DeepSeek-R1 reasoning traces over retrieved docs (t0-1.1-k5-32B) matches frontier models on condition accuracy.
 number: 0.56 condition (k=5) vs Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct 0.54 with RAG and 0.38 without; GPT-4o 0.56; o3-mini 0.57; DeepSeek-R1 0.56; s1.1-32B 0.49; Qwen3-32B 0.53. Disposition: t0 0.51, Qwen+RAG 0.50, o3-mini 0.56.
 setup: 1,000 synthetic NHS A-to-Z queries (GPT-4o written), 989 condition pages, k=5 retrieved summaries, average of 10 runs, SD about 0.01. Trained on 2,000 synthetic traces.
 quote: "Our t0-1.1-k5-32B, which has been fine-tuned on in-domain reasoning examples, further increases the accuracy in determining the correct condition, with an almost 20% performance improvement compared to the base Qwen model and an additional small improvement against using retrieval alone."
 where: Table 2, p.24 (offset about 56,500-58,000)
 Caution for the note: the gain over retrieval alone is only 0.54 to 0.56, within about 2 SD. Most of the gain comes from retrieval (0.38 to 0.54).

2. Retrieval caps accuracy, because the reader only sees the top k.
 number: k=5 gives p@5 = 0.76, so the maximum condition accuracy is 76%. p@30 = 0.93.
 setup: summaries indexed, all-mpnet-base-v2, Chroma, 1,000 queries.
 quote: "Note, however, that this choice imposes a maximum achievable prediction accuracy of 76%, since the reasoner only considers the retrieved documents as potentially relevant."
 where: p.21, Table 1
 Related: LLM reranking and ReAct-style query rephrasing "did not consistently lead to significant improvements in our setting."

3. Indexing LLM-written summaries beat indexing full pages for this task.
 number: p@1 0.51 vs 0.47; p@5 0.76 vs 0.68; p@10 0.83 vs 0.78; p@100 0.98 vs 0.94. Summaries cut length by 85%. Full pages: 5,824 chunks; summaries: 989 documents.
 setup: summaries by Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct, prompted to keep only symptoms and next steps, so the summary is tuned to the query type.
 quote: "Full pages 5 824 0.47 0.68 0.78 0.87 0.91 0.94 / Summaries 989 0.51 0.76 0.83 0.93 0.96 0.98"
 where: Table 1, p.21. The authors say "For a more general retrieval system ... it may be more advisable to index full pages."

4. Full-document retrieval inflates training and context length, and summarisation fixes it.
 number: 74,641 average tokens per training example (5 full docs), reduced to 7,544 with summaries. For comparison, s1K is 9,109 and s1K-1.1 is 26,969.
 quote: "the average token length of the training examples using the Qwen2.5 tokenizer was 74 641" and "the average token length of our reasoning traces was reduced to 7 544."
 where: pp.13, offsets about 29,500-31,000

5. Small models get most of their gain from reasoning training, large models from reading ability.
 number: Table 4 condition accuracy with k=5: 1.5B 0.53, 3B 0.56, 7B 0.54, 14B 0.56, 32B 0.56; Qwen2.5-32B baseline 0.54; R1-671B 0.56. Memory at 16-bit: 1.5B 3 GB, 3B 6 GB, 32B 64 GB, 671B 1,342 GB. Disposition stays 0.47-0.51.
 quote: "even a 1.5B parameter model maintains performance comparable to a 32B parameter non-reasoning model, especially in condition prediction" and "for leaner models (1.5B and 3B), a large performance boost is given by in-domain reasoning training which offers this interpretation ability that was otherwise lacking."
 where: Table 4 and Fig 5, pp.27-28. The exact 1.5B and 3B Qwen+RAG values are only in Fig 5 and are not given in text.
 Memory formula: "GPU memory needed (bytes)= 2 × Number of parameters".

6. In-domain reasoning beats a general reasoning model (s1.1) of the same size.
 number: Table 3 (single run): basic 0.52/0.64 vs 0.49/0.52; hypochondriac 0.62/0.44 vs 0.52/0.37; downplay 0.53/0.47 vs 0.47/0.43 (condition/disposition). s1.1 is "3 to 12% worse"; "over a 40% increase in underestimation errors" for s1.1 on basic queries.
 quote: "a general-purpose reasoning model such as s1.1 performs 3 to 12% worse, depending on the query type and evaluation metric."
 where: Table 3, p.26. Single run, so no variance.

7. Generic reasoning fine-tuning hurts below a size threshold.
 number: the benefit appears at 14B and above on AIME24; at 1.5B fine-tuning lowers performance.
 quote: "the benefit of reasoning capabilities emerge clearly when adopting models with at least 14B parameters, while for smaller models (1.5B), the fine-tuning process ends up negatively impacting model performance."
 where: Sec 3.2.1, p.10, Fig 2. Maths benchmark, no budget forcing.

8. Retrieval's effect varies by model and task.
 number: GPT-4o condition 0.49 to 0.56 but disposition 0.56 to 0.54 (down); o3-mini condition 0.27 to 0.57 with retrieval.
 quote: "GPT-4o sees its performance slightly decreasing, potentially due to more ambiguity from the amount of information now available."
 where: p.23-24. The o3-mini explanation: it "loses focus ... and ends up considering too many possible scenarios" without evidence.

9. Distillation sets a ceiling: disposition did not reach o3-mini.
 quote: "the reasoning traces provided by DeekSeek-R1, which set the limit of expertise that can be distilled into smaller models"
 where: p.24. The authors say "We believe", so this is an untested explanation.

10. Design choices.
 - Context goes in the system prompt, not the user turn, so it does not accumulate in history. Quote: "We chose not to do this to limit the growth of the conversation history context length" (p.14).
 - Retrieval is a tool call, so follow-ups like "Where can I buy them?" get a rewritten query, and "Hello" skips retrieval. Qwen2.5-Instruct-32B is the agent because it was "more consistent for tool-calling"; t0 does generation (p.16).
 - History is trimmed by tokens, the system prompt is never dropped (p.15).
 - Fine-tuning recipe: 5 epochs, lr 1e-5 cosine, block size 32,768, bf16, FSDP, 2,000 traces, 16 A100 80GB, about 80 GPU-hours for the final 32B model (pp.9, 22). Total project compute is about 700 + 500 + 2,500 GPU-hours.
 - Budget forcing at evaluation: maximum 1,024 tokens, end-of-thinking suppressed up to 3 times (footnote 21, p.23).

LIMITS
- Synthetic queries from GPT-4o, with only a subset reviewed by a clinician. One domain (NHS pages), one retriever. Authors state it is "not intended as a tool for providing medical advice."
- Absolute accuracy is low (0.56 condition, about 0.5 disposition).
- No hallucination metric, and no faithfulness or citation evaluation, although the paper claims hallucination reduction.
- No ablation of fine-tuning with traces vs fine-tuning on answers only. No comparison of RAG+SFT vs RAG alone at the same model, beyond 0.54 vs 0.56.
- Table 3 is a single run.
- Summaries were tuned to the task. Authors say users "should assess" retrieval impact.
- Teacher trace quality caps the student.
- No authentication in the demo. Traces from a frontier model need a different plan for private data (manual traces or a local teacher).
- The dated part is the baseline models (Qwen2.5, s1.1, Qwen3-32B, o3-mini, 2025).

BUILDS ON
- s1: Muennighoff et al., "s1: Simple test-time scaling", arXiv:2501.19393, 2025 (SFT recipe on 1K traces, budget forcing).
- DeepSeek-R1, Guo et al., arXiv:2501.12948, 2025 (teacher and distillation).
- Snell et al., ICLR 2025 (test-time compute).
- Wei et al., NeurIPS 2022 (chain of thought).
- Lewis et al., 2020 (RAG, ref [9]).
- Yao et al., ReAct, ICLR 2023.
- REPLUG (Shi et al.) and MemGPT.
- Karpukhin et al., DPR, EMNLP 2020.
- Sentence-Transformers (ref [51]).
- Contextual retrieval (ref [33]).
- Gemma 2 distillation.
- Qwen2.5 and Qwen3.

CODE: No code worth keeping. Qwen chat format (p.14): "<|im_start|>{role}\n{content}<|im_end|>". The retrieval-prompt template is in A.1 (pp.36-37). It includes "If the retrieved context is not relevant to the patient's query, you should also say that you don't know." The agent prompt is in A.2. The summarisation prompt is in A.3, and the reasoning-trace prompt is in A.5.

FIGURES (candidates)
- Fig 5 (p.28): condition accuracy of Qwen alone vs +RAG vs t0, by size. It shows the main teaching point: reasoning training matters most for small models. The values are not in the text, so it needs the image.
- Fig 3 (p.16): conversational RAG with an agent that either calls the retriever or answers directly, then the reasoning model generates.
- Fig 4 (p.17): the full pipeline (synthetic data, retrieval, traces, fine-tuning).
- Fig 2 (p.11): AIME24 by model size, base vs distilled.
- Fig 1 (p.5): standard RAG pipeline, generic.
- Fig 6 (p.29): chat UI, low value.

FIT TO NOTES (generative-ai/02-rag-retrieval/notes/06-generation-for-rag.md)
- The note cites Chan nowhere (grep for chan, t0-1, 2508.11386 and lean finds no match in note 06 or references.md). The claims are new.
- Best slot: the "RAG vs fine-tuning" section (line 521), right after the RARE sentence (line 530) and before the RAFT paragraph (line 532). It is the same "fine-tune with retrieved documents in the prompt, using reasoning traces distilled from a larger model" pattern as RARE. Chan adds a small-model, on-prem, no-human-labels variant and the finding that the gain over plain RAG is small at 32B and large at 1.5-3B.
- Secondary slots: "Choosing an LLM" (model size vs retrieval; GPT-4o disposition falls with RAG, o3-mini condition accuracy rises from 0.27 to 0.57); the context-budget section (summarising docs by 85% before putting them in the context); the retrieval-as-a-tool pattern (note 08 agentic RAG, which grep did not check); the failure-mode list (line 567).
- The note's existing claim "RAG adds knowledge; fine-tuning changes behaviour" is sharpened, not contradicted. Here retrieval supplies most of the accuracy and reasoning fine-tuning supplies the ability to read it, strongest in the 1.5-3B models.
- Add a references.md row.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. Fig 2 and Fig 5 numbers are not extractable from text. The extraction merges some words (e.g. "ons1"), which does not affect the numbers.
